clue.text: Bomb Wallis' other half with game crossing

parts.note: Barnes Wallis designed the bouncing bomb; his first name is the other half of Wallis
the card game

explanation.surface: An engineer's bomb and a game get mixed up in one odd sentence about Wallis and his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is the Boat Race; Barnes Bridge is a railway bridge over the Thames on the course. 'Crossing' doubles as a hint at the game, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge is a structure carrying a road or railway over a river, so this landmark is a crossing of the Thames.

clue.text: See 14
Hope country will indiscriminately ruin art with AI

indicators.note: acting without choosing an order, the letters are thrown together at random

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'with' adds them on

explanation.surface: A warning that careless use of artificial intelligence will wreck art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' is not the feeling but Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom invented by the novelist Anthony Hope for his adventure stories.

clue.text: Island turned up in toy exhibition

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upwards means the letters read from bottom to top
the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A toy island appears at a toy show.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot (also ait) is a small island in a river, a word used especially of islets in the Thames.

clue.text: Waster had drug instead of black tie

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, swapping one for the other

parts.note: a deadbeat is a lazy, idle person
H is slang for heroin
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A layabout turned up drugged instead of wearing black tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black tie' reads as a dress code, but 'tie' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race in which two competitors finish exactly level, which is a tie.

clue.text: Sad missing rioting archdeacons invade

indicators.note: a riot throws everything into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
something missing is left out, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Unhappy clergy, having missed out, storm in angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude gradually on another's territory or rights, a synonym for invade.

clue.text: See 29
Lapsed religion has little light to shine

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: a little of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lapsed believer finds a small light to show the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' and 'to' join the pieces; CE, the Church of England, is a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstandingly good at something, which is what shining in a field means.

clue.text: Doctor has met runner

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor has met an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the signal to rearrange. A runner is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river on which the Boat Race is rowed, and rivers run, so a runner is a river.

clue.text: Police's melancholy uniform music
Blow to make chilling song trendy

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
cool means fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy song gives you chills.
explanation.definitionFit: To air-cool something is to lower its temperature by blowing air across it, as with an engine.

clue.text: Party Leader caught in trap — a test for humanity

indicators.note: something caught in a trap ends up inside it

parts.note: a catch is a trap or snare

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party leader is caught in a trap that tests their humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: The P goes inside CATCH after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A CAPTCHA is the online puzzle websites set to check that a user is a human and not a bot.

clue.text: Judge pace

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to assess or evaluate

explanation.walkthrough: Pace in rowing is measured as a stroke rate, a nod to the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate works as a verb meaning to evaluate and as a noun meaning a speed or tempo.

clue.text: Crane exhibition that is holding auction

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration or display

indicators.note: something holding another thing wraps around it

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
to auction is to sell

explanation.surface: A building crane is on display at a show that hosts an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane' looks like machinery; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The demoiselle is a small species of crane, a bird of Eurasian grasslands.

clue.text: Cute boy narrative is misplaced in long rivalry

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet coming-of-age story is out of place in a tale of long-standing rivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge have contested the University Boat Race on the Thames since 1829, a famously long rivalry.

clue.text: Film containing an Afghan, maybe

indicators.note: one word containing another holds it inside

parts.note: cine relates to film
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film featuring someone from Afghanistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afghan' reads as a person; it is the hound.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghan hound is one breed of dog, so it is an example of something canine, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Head off irritating auditor's first haunting

indicators.note: with its head off a word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a CA, chartered accountant, may serve as an auditor, and comes first
an itchy jumper is irritating

explanation.surface: A tune keeps nagging at an auditor even when he takes his head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor's first' looks like a first-letter signal, but it means the auditor goes first; CA stands for chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune sticks in the mind, just as a haunting melody lingers in the memory.

clue.text: Beach defences rolled up when danger looms

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the steel anti-tank obstacles placed on beaches in the Second World War
second meaning: the spiny animals that curl into a ball under threat

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic description of the animals rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Czech hedgehogs were crossed steel girders blocking landing craft, and the small mammal protects itself by rolling into a prickly ball.

clue.text: Killer of animals at home

parts.note: two asses, donkeys, are the animals
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone who kills livestock on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'animals' supplies two donkeys side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially one who kills a prominent person.

clue.text: Hands out reward rejected by antagonists

parts.note: fists are clenched hands

parts.note: one's due is what one has earned

explanation.surface: Rivals spurn the prize being handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudists are people engaged in a bitter, long-running quarrel, so they are opponents or antagonists.

clue.text: Ask opinion on reduced sail

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, losing its final letter

parts.note: to canvass is to seek people's views, as election campaigners do

explanation.surface: Someone asks for views on cutting back on sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas is the heavy cloth that sails were traditionally made of, so it stands for a sail.

clue.text: See 1 across
Test maiden's recorder

parts.note: surface reading: a young woman tries out her recorder, the wind instrument
setter's reading: the official at a Test match who logs each maiden over, a cricket over with no runs conceded

explanation.surface: A girl tries out her recorder.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match and a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorer is the official who records every ball, run and maiden in a cricket match.

clue.text: Starts to discover every landowner had invaded Indian territory

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: History's starting point: learning that every landowner had invaded Indian lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is a union territory of India containing the capital New Delhi.

clue.text: Alter a crew to make a real difference

indicators.note: the preceding letters are worked into a different word, which is what they go on to make

parts.note: taken as written; the instruction word alter also lends its letters

explanation.surface: Changing the crew makes a real difference to the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alter' reads as the anagram signal but is part of the fodder. In rowing, clear water is open space between the leading boat's stern and the chaser's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear water is a decisive gap or lead between competitors, a real difference in position.

clue.text: Number 27
Bow at start of big finish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Taking a bow at the start of a grand finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' reads as the front of a boat, apt in a rowing puzzle, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow is to bend the body forward, so bend is a synonym.

explanation.definitionFit: Crew prefixes both a close-cropped hairstyle and a plain round-necked jumper style.

clue.text: Gets back controls restricting the state

parts.note: reins are the means of controlling a horse
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

clue.text: Where to find posh merchandise organised, or try roadside shop

indicators.note: things organised are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on where to buy upmarket goods: get organised, or try a roadside stall.

clue.text: Call about damaged tyre having another crack

clue.text: Misrepresents taunts around Primary School

parts.note: the first letter of the word
